summary.headline: Q4 FY26 PAT rose over 6x YoY to INR 340 Crore (ROA 4.4%, ROE 17.8%) while FY26 credit cost hit 6.74%, above the 5.5-6.0% guidance.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 showed a sharp recovery: AUM grew 14.0% YoY and 11.4% QoQ, disbursements rose 28.4% YoY to INR 8,313 Crore, and PPOP grew 23.1% YoY to INR 780 Crore. Full-year FY26 PAT was INR 778 Crore (ROA 2.7%, ROE 10.7%), with credit cost at 6.74% versus 5.5-6.0% guidance, including 0.64% from ECL rate increases (INR 39 Crore extra in Q4 for West Asia-related scenarios). Retail finance rose to 18.1% of AUM from 5.9% a year earlier. Management issued FY27 guidance of 20-25% AUM growth, NIM 12.8-13.2%, credit cost 3.0-4.0%, and ROA 4.0-4.8%, and launched "Project Shakti" as a 10-year framework.

financial_highlights.change: In line with annual growth guidance despite 7.6% write-offs in FY26
60 bps reduction during FY26; marginal cost about 8.9%
More than 6x YoY, +34.7% QoQ; ROA 4.4%, ROE 17.8%

financial_highlights.value: 6.74% (6.10% from new PAR, 0.64% from ECL rate increase)
CAR 24.4%, total equity INR 7,842 Crore, debt-equity 3.0x

segments.name: Group loans (MFI)
segments.commentary: Unique group loan borrowers are 46.1% of AUM (up from 26.6% in Aug 2024). Management guides MFI AUM growth of 10-12% in FY27, with 6-8% of customers graduating to retail each year.

segments.name: Retail finance
segments.commentary: Share of AUM rose to 18.1% (March 2026) from 5.9% a year ago. Management targets roughly 24-25% of AUM by end FY27. Individual business loans run under Unnati (avg ticket about INR 1.7 lakh) and Unnati Lite (INR 75,000-1 lakh).

segments.name: Mortgage loans
segments.commentary: About 120 dedicated retail branches. Management says standalone mortgage branches break even at a mortgage book of roughly INR 800-1,000 Crore. Mortgage is the only retail product not yet profitable at product level.

guidance_outlook: FY27 AUM growth 20-25%, NIM 12.8-13.2%, cost-to-income 33-35%, credit cost 3.0-4.0%, ROA 4.0-4.8%, ROE 16-20%.
MFI growth 10-12% in FY27; retail (non-MFI) supplies the balance of AUM growth.
Cost of borrowing seen as bottoming out, likely range-bound or slightly higher; no MFI rate hike planned unless borrowing costs move significantly (two-quarter lag).
ECL provisioning expected to stay around the 1.63% Stage 1 level; management says rates will be reviewed quarterly by a Board-level ECL committee.
Cost-to-income guidance includes inflationary buffers linked to global issues; management said it may not rise if global issues do not prolong.
New-customer share of MFI disbursements expected to rise from about 20% in FY26 to 30-40% at steady state.
capex_capacity: Branches rose by 183 in FY26 to 2,236 as of March 2026; employee base grew 4.6% YoY to 21,941, with attrition at 29.4% (33.5% a year earlier).
Grameen Mahi app onboarded 8.4 lakh borrowers in FY26, taking the active base to 11.2 lakh (25.4% of borrowers); digital collections rose to 22% of Q4 FY26 from 14% in Q4 FY25.
Technology processes over 30 lakh transactions a day, with 70,000-80,000 loan applications and 20-25 lakh bureau submissions daily.
Collections management platform piloted with predictive next-best-action decisioning; internal audit frequency raised from 60 to 40 days.
demand_pricing: Borrower additions: 3.3 lakh in Q4 and 9.8 lakh in FY26 (38% new to credit); management said 976,000 customers were added in FY26 against 491,000 write-offs.

Pricing is set against borrowing, operating and credit costs; with credit cost falling, management expects some pricing pass-through to customers, which is why FY27 NIM guidance is lower than Q4's 14.2%.
Management sees no MFI rate hike for now; PAR accretion is stable through April and early May 2026.

Competition in Tamil Nadu from peers entering individual loans; management argues execution and existing customer base (about INR 30,000 Crore already in portfolio, INR 40,000 Crore outside) are the edge.
Yield on MFI and non-MFI products is close, except home loans (small book, to be done via partnerships).

qa_highlights.question: Why is the FY27 credit cost guidance so wide at 3.0-4.0%, and how much is from higher ECL provisioning?
qa_highlights.answer: Nilesh Dalvi said the new ECL model (Stage 1 at 1.63%) already prices in global risks. The range reflects uncertainty over the West Asia fallout. April and early May PAR accretion is stable, so the company may land at the lower or higher end.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 3-4% credit cost guidance conservative, given PAR accretion is under 10 bps?
qa_highlights.answer: Ganesh Narayanan said Q4 is normally the lowest-accretion quarter after an elevated credit cost period. The range also includes a normal one-month accretion rate, heatwave risk and external events.

qa_highlights.question: Will MFI growth shift toward individual loans, and is the 60-40 MFI/non-MFI mix a constraint over 10 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said graduating 6-8% of customers a year into individual loans is a clear path, with retail lending at 2-3x MFI exposure per customer. Over time, the 60-40 limit could be handled through securitisation, portfolio sales, co-lending or inorganic moves.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the NIM decline in guidance, and will cost-to-income rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Nilesh Dalvi said lower NIM reflects expected pass-through of lower credit costs, and a buffer on borrowing costs as domestic rates may reverse. Cost-to-income guidance includes inflation buffers and may not rise if global issues ease.

qa_highlights.question: Breakdown of product-level profitability in retail?
qa_highlights.answer: Except mortgages, all retail products are profitable at product level. Mortgage standalone branches are expected to break even at a book of INR 800-1,000 Crore.

qa_highlights.question: How much of MFI disbursement goes to new vs existing customers?
qa_highlights.answer: About 20% new and 80% existing in FY26; management expects a steady state of 30-40% new customers, reached over time.

risks_watch: Credit cost guidance of 3.0-4.0% depends on how the West Asia crisis, fuel or gas supply, and heatwaves play out; management called out a prolonged supply disruption as a risk.
ECL provisions are set quarterly by a Board committee; any reversal of the 1.63% Stage 1 rate would move credit cost and ROA.
Cost-to-income guidance of 33-35% assumes inflation; a rise in input costs would push it higher.
Borrowing costs have bottomed; hedging costs have risen internationally, and a reversal in domestic rates is expected over 3-4 quarters.
Retail ramp-up needs a 24-25% AUM share by FY27-end, competition in individual loans (e.g., Tamil Nadu), and the 60-40 MFI/non-MFI regulatory mix in the longer term.
Next quarter: watch whether PAR accretion holds in normal range, and whether the ECL rate is kept at 1.63%.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the recovery and FY27 growth, but cautious on credit cost and cost-to-income, where management kept wide ranges and explicit buffers for the West Asia crisis. Answers on the 60-40 mix and long-term regulation were direct but open-ended.
key_quotes: Q4 FY26 marks a decisive inflection in our performance trajectory.
We prioritized collections first, then portfolio maintenance and only then growth.
The new ECL model aligns with our conservative provisioning approach as our loan book scales over medium term.
Our model has become more resilient with every passing crisis.

adds.what: Branches rose by 183 in FY26 to 2,236 as of March 2026 (historical, not forward-guided)
About 120 dedicated mortgage retail branches (existing, not new additions)

growth.why: FY27 guidance of 20-25% AUM growth (midpoint 22.5%) with NIM 12.8-13.2%, backed by Q4 disbursements up 28.4% YoY to INR 8,313 Crore, 9.8 lakh borrower additions and retail rising to 18.1% of AUM, but no new capacity or order book was quantified, so backing is partial.
